pl-l3d23c9-d1e115.summary: Concludes from the preceding that faith alone is rightly called the foundation of all virtues and good works.
claims: Faith alone is the foundation of all virtues and good works.

pl-l3d23c9-d1e118.summary: Qualifies the claim: faith is not the foundation of charity, since charity is the cause of the virtue of faith, not the reverse. Charity is the cause and mother of all virtues, without which all else is had in vain; and, as established earlier, charity is the Holy Spirit, so no virtue causes it.
claims: Faith is not the foundation of charity.
Charity causes the virtue of faith.
Charity is the mother and cause of all virtues.
Charity is the Holy Spirit, and so no virtue is its cause.

pl-l3d23c9-d1e124.summary: Augustine on charity's preeminence among the Church's gifts, like oil that cannot be pressed down but rises to the top; therefore faith is not its cause or foundation.
claims: Charity excels all the gifts of the Church.
Faith is not the cause or foundation of charity.

pl-l3d23c9-d1e140.summary: Presents a counter-authority: Gregory on Ezekiel says that unless faith is first held, spiritual love is not reached; faith precedes charity, since no one can love what they have not believed, just as they cannot hope for it.
claims: Gregory holds that faith precedes charity.
No one can love or hope for what has not been believed.

pl-l3d23c9-d1e152.summary: Resolves the tension: Gregory's statement can refer to faith that is not a virtue (unformed faith, which often precedes hope and charity), or to the act of faith, which perhaps naturally precedes the act of charity as it does the act of hope; Gregory's added words ('unless you believe what you hear, you will not be inflamed to love it') support this, concerning only things not seen.
claims: Unformed faith frequently precedes hope and charity.
The act of faith perhaps naturally precedes the act of charity.
Gregory's statement does not make the virtue of faith the cause of charity.

pl-l3d23c9-d1e158.summary: Chrysostom: faith makes unseen things subsist in the soul; faith properly concerns these, since seen things are objects of recognition, not faith.
claims: Faith makes unseen things subsist in the soul.
Seen things are objects of recognition, not of faith.

pl-l3d23c9-d1e164.summary: Augustine (De praedestinatione sanctorum): to believe is nothing other than to think with assent.
claims: To believe is to think with assent.

pl-l3d23c9.summary: Explains why faith alone is called the foundation of all virtues and good works, while denying that it is the foundation or cause of charity: charity, which is the Holy Spirit, is the cause and mother of all virtues, including faith. Gregory's dictum that faith precedes charity is interpreted as referring either to unformed faith or to the natural priority of the act of faith, since no one can love what they have not believed. Authorities from Chrysostom and Augustine close the chapter on faith's object and act.
claims: Faith alone is the foundation of all virtues and good works.
Faith is not the cause or foundation of charity; charity is the cause of faith as a virtue.
Charity is the Holy Spirit and the mother of all virtues.
Gregory's claim that faith precedes charity applies to unformed faith or to the natural priority of acts.
To believe is to think with assent.
